text:
maria: Heads up — acme-analytics reported a spate of 401s for signed callbacks after an IdP key rotation. They said it started ~10:20 UTC and affects our edged API nodes.

kevin: Can you paste the exact error they're seeing? 401s could be exp/nbf, kid mismatch, or signature fail.

support-agent: From the customer: "signature verification failed: invalid signature (jose)" and also a few "token_expired" in their logs. They mentioned their IdP had a maintenance window and likely rotated keys.

maria: Sample log they sent: 
```
2026-02-14T10:23:11Z auth: verify_jwt failed issuer=https://idp.acme/ err="jose: crypto/rsa: verification error" kid="pkey_v3"
2026-02-14T10:24:02Z auth: verify_jwt failed issuer=https://idp.acme/ err="token is expired" aud=redwood-api
```

lenore: Two separate things. The rsa verification error suggests our JWKS cache had stale keys (kid not found or wrong key material). The token_expired suggests clock skew at the issuer or client. The customer also said their servers had a clock jump during maintenance.

samir: Did our JWKS fetch logs show any upstream 5xx or DNS failures around that time? If our cache couldn't refresh after rotation, edge nodes would keep serving the old key.

maria: I checked edge logs (excerpt): 
```
2026-02-14T10:15:00Z jwks-cache: hit issuer=https://idp.acme/ ttl=00:14:59
2026-02-14T10:20:25Z jwks-cache: refresh start issuer=https://idp.acme/
2026-02-14T10:20:25Z jwks-fetch: GET https://idp.acme/.well-known/jwks.json -> error: dial tcp: i/o timeout
2026-02-14T10:20:25Z jwks-cache: refresh failed, retaining old keys
```

kevin: That matches. Customer rotated keys around 10:19, our refresh timed out. Then their client clock jumped forward ~6 minutes which made a few tokens show as expired when verified against now(). Combined causes -> intermittent 401s and some signature mismatches if kid changed.

support-agent: They asked for repro steps to get engineering a deterministic test.

lenore: Repro steps for infra:
1) Simulate JWKS rotation: create a new RSA keypair, publish new jwks.json with kid=new_kid, keep old jwks available for a brief overlap.
2) Configure one of our edge nodes with a locked-in old cache (prevent refresh) or simulate jwks fetch failure via /etc/hosts -> 127.0.0.1 for idp host.
3) Issue tokens signed with new_kid and send requests -> observe verification fails.
4) Also simulate client clock jump: on client VM run `sudo date -s "+6 minutes"` and resend tokens that were freshly minted to trigger exp/nbf rejections.

samir: Examples for token generation and request: 
```bash
# sign with new key (client side repro)
jwt_header='{"alg":"RS256","kid":"new_kid"}'
# payload has exp in 5m
# use openssl/jwt lib to sign...
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $JWT" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/callbacks
```

maria: Short-term mitigation we advised the customer: add small leeway to token verification (e.g., 60s) and retry on 401 for 1 minute, and we can trigger a JWKS refresh on our side.

kevin: Long-term we should consider: reduce default JWKS TTL, add jittered background refresh + exponential backoff, and add admin endpoint to force refresh per-issuer. Also log metrics when jwks-fetch timeouts spike.

lenore: We already have a per-issuer admin refresh endpoint but it's internal-only: `POST /_admin/issuers/refresh-jwks?issuer=https://idp.acme/`. I can run that to push new keys to all edges.

maria: Please run it now and tell the customer to retry after ~30s.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: Triggering JWKS refresh for issuer=https://idp.acme/ across 12 edge nodes. Job id=jb-8891.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: Completed refresh job jb-8891. 12/12 nodes updated.

support-agent: Customer retried and reports requests are now succeeding. They still saw a handful of expired tokens; suggested increasing client clock sync checks.

kevin: Action items:
- lenore: add alert when jwks-fetch timeout rate > 5/min for any issuer. (owner: lenore)
- samir: add a forced-refresh admin API doc note and small playbook. (owner: samir)
- eng-runtime: evaluate lowering jwks-cache TTL to 5m with async refresh. (owner: kevin)
- support-agent: send customer postmortem with suggested mitigations (leeway, retries, NTP checks). (owner: support-agent)

maria: Thanks team. I'll leave this thread open until we have the alerts and the playbook. :white_check_mark: 

support-agent: Customer follow-up: "Thanks, flushing worked. We'll harden our NTP config and avoid maintenance jumps." :thumbsup:
